<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Therefore the context test cannot be selected by a policy that strictly
maximizes one-step information gain:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="x^{\mathrm{ctx}}\notin\arg\max_{x}Q_{1}(b_{0},x),\qquad Q_{1}(b,x)=I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid b,x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>ctx</mi></msup><mo>∉</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mi>max</mi><mi>x</mi></munder><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{\mathrm{ctx}}\notin\arg\max_{x}Q_{1}(b_{0},x),\qquad Q_{1}(b,x)=I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid b,x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Thus a myopic information-gain objective assigns no credit to the context test,
despite the fact that observing the context identifies which subsequent tests
are informative.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A two-step objective assigns value to the context test.</span>
For a two-step policy, define</p>
<table id="A2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Q_{2}(b,x)=I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid b,x)+\gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p(y\mid b,x)}\left[V_{1}(b^{x,y})\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{2}(b,x)=I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid b,x)+\gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p(y\mid b,x)}\left[V_{1}(b^{x,y})\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.2" class="ltx_p">where</p>
<table id="A2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="V_{1}(b^{\prime})=\max_{x^{\prime}}I(\Theta;Y_{x^{\prime}}\mid b^{\prime},x^{\prime})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></munder><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{1}(b^{\prime})=\max_{x^{\prime}}I(\Theta;Y_{x^{\prime}}\mid b^{\prime},x^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.3" class="ltx_p">is the value of the best remaining one-step experiment, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b^{x,y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^{x,y}</annotation></semantics></math>
denotes the belief state after observing outcome <math id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> from test <math id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">For the context test, the first term is zero. However, observing its outcome
reveals <math id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, and therefore identifies the relevant block of disease tests.
Consequently,</p>
<table id="A2.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{2}(b_{0},x^{\mathrm{ctx}})=\gamma\mathbb{E}_{C}\left[\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{C}}I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid C)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>ctx</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>C</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{2}(b_{0},x^{\mathrm{ctx}})=\gamma\mathbb{E}_{C}\left[\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{C}}I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid C)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p11.1" class="ltx_p">If every context contains at least one disease-informative test,</p>
<table id="A2.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{c}}I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid C=c)&gt;0\qquad\forall c," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mspace style="width:2.167em;" width="2.167em"></mspace><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}_{c}}I(\Theta;Y_{x}\mid C=c)&gt;0\qquad\forall c,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p11.2" class="ltx_p">then</p>
<table id="A2.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{Q_{2}(b_{0},x^{\mathrm{ctx}})&gt;0.}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>ctx</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{Q_{2}(b_{0},x^{\mathrm{ctx}})&gt;0.}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS2.p12.1" class="ltx_p">Hence, although the context test has zero one-step information value, it has
strictly positive two-step information value through the future experiment
that it enables.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.3.3 </span>Predicting target attributes from the questioning history</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Setup.</span>
To assess whether multi-step training also benefits predictions about an unknown target, we evaluate the animal-trained <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> reasoning policies on the TwentyQuestions dataset of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2025)</a></cite>. This is a separate object-domain evaluation using the dataset’s annotated target questions, not the animal contrastive set used for training. Each policy plays up to 20 turns for 50 test objects. Before questioning and after each completed turn, we ask it to predict the answers to 15 fixed attribute questions about the hidden object from the history alone. We score the labels <span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Yes</span>, <span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">No</span>, <span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Often</span>, and <span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Sometimes</span>, normalizing their model likelihoods and taking the most likely answer. Probe scoring disables reasoning, does not reveal the target, and does not feed the probe answers back into the game.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We sample five probe questions per difficulty group for each object. Difficulty is defined by the frequency of the object’s correct answer to that question across the dataset: easy answers occur with frequency at least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math>, medium answers with frequency in <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0.3,0.5)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0.3,0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>, and hard answers with frequency below <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.3</annotation></semantics></math>. These are disjoint groups in our evaluation. We use three evaluation seeds, with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> for the multi-step policies, and report mean accuracy and SEM across repeats. These repeats evaluate fixed trained checkpoints rather than independent training runs. Games stop when solved or invalid, so later-turn averages include only games that reach that turn.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-step policies improve target prediction during parts of the trajectory.</span>
Figure <a href="#A2.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ B.3.3 Predicting target attributes from the questioning history ‣ B.3 Non-myopic information acquisition ‣ Appendix B Extended Experimental Results ‣ Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows the clearest gains on medium and hard target questions. The <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> policy generally improves medium-question accuracy, while <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> improves hard-question accuracy over much of the trajectory. Overall accuracy at turn five is <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math>, compared with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="29.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>29.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math>. The advantage is not uniform: at turn 20 the corresponding overall accuracies are <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>43.4</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>43.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="43.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>43.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">43.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>. We therefore interpret these curves as evidence of improved intermediate target-attribute prediction, not uniformly higher final accuracy or target-identification solve rate. Because the policies generate their own histories, the comparison reflects both the information they gather and how they use it; it does not isolate prediction quality under identical evidence.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.20832v1/result2_hf_target_prediction.png" id="A2.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/170;" width="548" height="170" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span><span id="A2.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-step training can improve target-attribute prediction during questioning.</span> Accuracy on annotated target questions from TwentyQuestions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, grouped by answer-frequency difficulty and aggregated across groups. Each animal-trained policy generates its own object-game histories; probes are scored without reasoning or access to the target identity. Curves and bands show mean <math id="A2.F7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> SEM over three evaluation seeds. Later-turn averages use the games that reach that turn, rather than carrying forward predictions from completed games.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Why might a non-myopic objective help target prediction?</span>
For a history <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{h}(\theta)=p(\theta\mid h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{h}(\theta)=p(\theta\mid h)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the belief over targets. A one-step objective values a question through <math id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(\Theta;Y\mid h,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\Theta;Y\mid h,x)</annotation></semantics></math>. A two-step objective additionally considers the information obtainable after each possible answer:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Q_{2}^{\pi}(h,x)=I(\Theta;Y\mid h,x)+\gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p(y\mid h,x)}\left[V_{1}^{\pi}(h,x,y)\right],\qquad p(\theta\mid h,x,y)\propto b_{h}(\theta)\,p(y\mid\theta,x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{2}^{\pi}(h,x)=I(\Theta;Y\mid h,x)+\gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p(y\mid h,x)}\left[V_{1}^{\pi}(h,x,y)\right],\qquad p(\theta\mid h,x,y)\propto b_{h}(\theta)\,p(y\mid\theta,x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Both objectives depend on beliefs and likelihoods, but the continuation term additionally rewards questions according to how their possible answers shape future information acquisition. We hypothesize that this places stronger pressure on the policy to retain which targets remain plausible and which attributes distinguish them. Such information is also useful for predicting target attributes from the history. This is a possible explanation for the intermediate prediction gains, not a mechanism established by the probe evaluation alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.3.4 </span>Myopic versus non-myopic question selection in Twenty Questions</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Many BED approaches optimize a myopic objective because evaluating future designs is computationally demanding. In an idealized, noiseless Twenty Questions game with a uniform prior and unrestricted binary partitions, balanced questions motivate a greedy strategy. However, the availability of such queries depends on the structure of the query and hypothesis spaces <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nowak, 2011</a>)</cite>. An open-ended language interface does not ensure that a policy can propose a balanced, semantically meaningful question for every remaining hypothesis set. Questions can therefore differ both in immediate EIG and in how readily subsequent questions distinguish the surviving hypotheses. This is a possible source of non-myopic behavior, not a claim that natural-language tasks are intrinsically non-myopic.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Simulation protocol.</span>
We examine this empirically with GPT-5 candidate questions and continuations from sampled animal-game states. This simulation uses the Animals hypothesis space, separately from the object-domain target-prediction evaluation above. We sample 20 states at each prefix length <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\{0,1,2,3,4,6,8,10\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\{0,1,2,3,4,6,8,10\}</annotation></semantics></math>, propose four candidate first questions from the public history, and simulate eight continuations per candidate for up to five questions. The questioner does not see the active hypothesis set. We treat the active hypotheses <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> as uniform and use hard oracle-answer partitions to compute immediate EIG in bits:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{EIG}_{1}(h_{t},x)=\log_{2}|C_{t}|-\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\frac{|C_{t,a}|}{|C_{t}|}\log_{2}|C_{t,a}|," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{EIG}_{1}(h_{t},x)=\log_{2}|C_{t}|-\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\frac{|C_{t,a}|}{|C_{t}|}\log_{2}|C_{t,a}|,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{t,a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{t,a}</annotation></semantics></math> is the subset consistent with answer <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and empty subsets contribute zero. For longer horizons, each rollout samples a target uniformly from the active set, forces the candidate question at its first step, and then follows the GPT-5 policy. We estimate <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{EIG}_{n}(h_{t},x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{EIG}_{n}(h_{t},x)</annotation></semantics></math> by averaging the realized <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log_{2}|C_{t}|-\log_{2}|C_{t+n}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log_{2}|C_{t}|-\log_{2}|C_{t+n}|</annotation></semantics></math> over continuations. The plotted support analysis rescored the saved questions and answers against the 200-animal contrastive set; it did not regenerate the continuations. Accordingly, these are diagnostics within the sampled question space, not exact optimal planning values for that expanded set.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Immediate- and downstream-EIG rankings can differ.</span>
Figure <a href="#A2.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ B.3.4 Myopic versus non-myopic question selection in Twenty Questions ‣ B.3 Non-myopic information acquisition ‣ Appendix B Extended Experimental Results ‣ Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> compares the candidate selected by immediate EIG with that selected by estimated EIG over two to five questions. Agreement is roughly <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40\%</annotation></semantics></math> at turns 0–2 and rises to <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>70</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70\%</annotation></semantics></math> at turns 8–10. Figure <a href="#A2.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ B.3.4 Myopic versus non-myopic question selection in Twenty Questions ‣ B.3 Non-myopic information acquisition ‣ Appendix B Extended Experimental Results ‣ Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows the corresponding trade-off in remaining support. One-step selection leaves the fewest hypotheses after the first question, whereas two- and three-step selection leave fewer hypotheses at their respective downstream horizons: approximately <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>25.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.8</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>28.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28.0</annotation></semantics></math> after two questions and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>18.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18.0</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="A2.SS3.SSS4.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.3</annotation></semantics></math> after three. These patterns suggest opportunities for lookahead within the simulated questions, with greater agreement later in the game. The candidate rankings and selected-candidate comparisons use finite Monte Carlo estimates, so they do not establish the optimality of any policy; declining average EIG alone would likewise not establish adaptive submodularity or myopic optimality.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.20832v1/figures/candidate_agreement_by_t_source_ig_1.png" id="A2.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:428/245;" width="428" height="245" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span><span id="A2.F8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Immediate and downstream information objectives can select different questions.</span> Tie-aware agreement between the candidate maximizing one-step EIG and that maximizing estimated EIG over two to five questions, by history length in the GPT-5 animal-game simulation. Agreement increases at later turns but remains below one.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A2.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.20832v1/figures/expected_support_selection_barplot_by_horizon_cropped.png" id="A2.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/151;" width="548" height="151" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span><span id="A2.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lookahead selection trades immediate for later support reduction.</span> Mean active hypotheses after one, two, or three questions when the first question is selected by estimated <math id="A2.F9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{EIG}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{EIG}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.F9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{EIG}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{EIG}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math id="A2.F9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{EIG}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{EIG}_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, followed by GPT-5 continuations. Labels show differences from one-step selection. This is a candidate-selection diagnostic, not a comparison of the trained AR-BED policies.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.3.5 </span>Multi-step training modestly improves downstream information acquisition</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Setup.</span>
We compare <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>AR</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>BED</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>AR</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>BED</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>AR</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>BED</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> from the same 180 held-out animal-game states, excluding starting states that overlap training. The multi-step policies use <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>. To separate the training horizon <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> from the evaluation horizon <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>, we evaluate every policy over one, two, and three questions and report cumulative expected information gain divided by <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>. Differences from the <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math> policy are paired by evaluation repeat; uncertainty is SEM across three repeats, not across independently trained models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The benefit is small and concentrated at longer evaluation horizons.</span>
Figure <a href="#A2.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ B.3.5 Multi-step training modestly improves downstream information acquisition ‣ B.3 Non-myopic information acquisition ‣ Appendix B Extended Experimental Results ‣ Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows positive mean gains for both multi-step policies at horizons two and three. The <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> policy changes average EIG by <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0020" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0020</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0020</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0062" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0062</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0062</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0116" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0116</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0116</annotation></semantics></math> nats per question at horizons one, two, and three, respectively; the corresponding <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> differences are <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0057" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0057</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0057</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0070</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0070</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0080</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A2.SS3.SSS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=2</annotation></semantics></math> starts slightly below the myopic policy on immediate EIG but achieves the largest mean downstream gain. These modest improvements are consistent with the intended lookahead objective, while showing that increasing the training horizon does not monotonically improve acquisition. Together with Cube-NM, they distinguish learning a clear non-myopic strategy in a controlled environment from the smaller gains available in open-ended natural-language questioning.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F10" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.20832v1/result2_tq_downstream_gain.svg" id="A2.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:318/220;" width="318" height="220"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span><span id="A2.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Multi-step training improves mean downstream acquisition on Twenty Questions.</span> Cumulative expected information gain divided by evaluation horizon, relative to <math id="A2.F10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>AR</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>BED</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{AR\text{-}BED}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, from 180 matched held-out animal-game states. The evaluation horizons are one, two, and three questions, independently of the training horizon <math id="A2.F10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>. Differences are paired by evaluation repeat; error bars show SEM over three repeats.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Additional Experimental Details</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless otherwise stated, Twenty Questions evaluations use 50 target games per domain and seed, a 20-turn budget, stochastic decoding with temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, top-k 0, up to 1024 generated tokens for the questioner, three retries for malformed tool calls. Solve rate counts all games in the denominator, including invalid games. Full-game information gain is reported as the mean over games of cumulative realized information gain divided by the number of questions asked in that game. Standard errors are over 3 evaluation repeats.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Training Details</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All AR-BED policy checkpoints are LoRA adapters trained from <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">unsloth/gemma-4-E4B-it</span>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We generate animal-target games with GPT-5 and sample up to five intermediate states per game for a total of <math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1200</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1200</annotation></semantics></math> training states. Training targets and held-out animal evaluation targets are disjoint; the 200-animal contrastive set specifies the likelihood-based reward and is distinct from the set of sampled training targets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We use 4-bit loading, LoRA rank 16, LoRA alpha 32, no dropout, no LoRA bias, and target the query, key, value, output, gate, up, and down projection modules. Training uses GRPO with 8 rollouts per sample, batch size 128, <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0</annotation></semantics></math>, one policy update iteration per batch, learning rate <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>, AdamW 8-bit optimization, a cosine learning-rate schedule with 10 warmup steps, temperature 1.0 sampling, max prompt length 1024, max completion length 512, 250 optimization steps, and active-threshold filtering at 0.01. Evaluation repeats use different game target order / decoding seeds, not independent training seeds.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Prompts</h3>

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reasoning Twenty Questions policy prompt.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You are playing Twenty Questions.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Ask one informative question at a time by calling the `ask_question` tool.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The question must be answerable with "yes", "no", or "maybe".</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Call `ask_question` exactly once.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Do not output the question as ordinary text.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">The tool response contains both an answer and a status:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">- `Status: continue` means the exact hidden target has not yet been identified. Continue asking questions, even if the answer was "yes".</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">- `Status: solved` means the exact hidden target has been identified and the game is complete.</span>
</span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Twenty Questions user/history template.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><pre id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
System: &lt;REASONING_SYSTEM_PROMPT or DIRECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT&gt;

User:
Goal: Identify the hidden target in at most {max_turns} turns.
Category: {category}.

For each previous turn:
Assistant tool call: ask_question({"question": "&lt;question&gt;"})
Tool response:
Answer: &lt;yes/no/maybe&gt;
Status: continue
</pre>
</div>
</section>

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.25" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.25.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.26" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.26.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.27" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.27.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.28" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.28.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.p28" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.p28.1" class="ltx_p">State your reasoning.</span>

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Oracle likelihood prompt template.</h5>

<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">System:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">You are an impartial judge for the game of 20 Questions. Given a question and a list of guesses, output the likelihood of the answers "yes", "no", and "maybe" in a JSON format.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">User:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Guesses:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">{json list of guesses}</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Questions:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">{json list of questions}</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.11.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.12.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">For each question and each guess, estimate:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.13.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">p(answer | guess is the true hidden target, question)</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.14.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.15.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">where answer is one of:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.16.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p16" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p16.1" class="ltx_p">- "yes"</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.17.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p17.1" class="ltx_p">- "no"</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.18.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.19" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.19.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.20.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p20" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p20.1" class="ltx_p">Rules:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.21.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.21.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.21.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">

<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p21.1" class="ltx_p">- For each question/guess pair, the probabilities for "yes", "no", and "maybe" must sum to 1.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.22" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.22.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.22.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.22.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p22" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p22.1" class="ltx_p">- Use "maybe" when the question is ambiguous, underspecified, or depends on interpretation.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.23" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.23.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.24" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.24.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.24.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.24.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p24" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p24.1" class="ltx_p">In addition, return a "solved" field for each question/guess pair. "solved" should be true if the question directly guesses that exact hidden target.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.25" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.25.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.26" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.26.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p26" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.27" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.27.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p27" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p27.1" class="ltx_p">{</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.28" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.28.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.p29.1" class="ltx_p">    "&lt;guess&gt;": {"yes": 0.0, "no": 0.0, "maybe": 0.0, "solved": false}</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.30" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.30.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Belief-probe prompt template.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">System:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Based on all questions and answers so far, what is your single best guess for the hidden {category}? Return JSON only.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">User:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MediQ transfer prompt templates.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Question-policy system prompt:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">You are a medical doctor investigating a clinical case.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.5.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">First think through the available evidence and which missing feature would best distinguish the answer options. Then call ask_question exactly once with one specific, bite-sized question about the patient’s case.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.7.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">This is information gathering only; a separate model will make the final diagnosis after the question budget is exhausted. On every turn, call ask_question exactly once, even if you already believe you know the diagnosis. Never select A/B/C/D or provide a final diagnosis yourself.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.9.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Do not repeat a question already answered in the conversation. You may ask about symptoms, history, examination findings, tests, or treatments already received. Do not output the question as ordinary text or inside XML tags. The tool response contains the patient’s answer and Status: continue. Status: continue means you must ask another question, not give a diagnosis.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.10.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:376.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">A ’cannot answer’ response applies only to that particular question. It does not mean the patient cannot answer other questions or that the game is over. Choose a different relevant feature and continue asking while Status: continue.</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.11.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.12.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">User prompt:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.13.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">PATIENT INFORMATION: {initial_information}</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.14.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.15.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.16.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p17.1" class="ltx_p">B: {option B}</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.18.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.20.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.21.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p21" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.p21.1" class="ltx_p">Patient simulator prompt:</span>
</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.22" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.22.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.23" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.23.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">

</span></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.24" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.24.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;"></span></span><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.25" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:397.5pt;"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.25.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:397.5pt;">
