<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS4.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Thus, when the distribution of realized targets matches the contrastive prior,
the realized reward is a single-sample estimator whose conditional expectation
is exactly the one-step EIG under the finite contrastive model.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Expected reward.</span>
Because both the hypothesis space and observation space are enumerable, we can
instead perform this expectation explicitly:</p>
<table id="A4.Ex26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}p_{C}(\theta_{\ell}\mid h_{t-1})\sum_{y}p(y\mid\theta_{\ell},x_{t})\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta_{\ell},x_{t})}{p_{C}(y\mid h_{t-1},x_{t})}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>exp</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>y</mi></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{L}p_{C}(\theta_{\ell}\mid h_{t-1})\sum_{y}p(y\mid\theta_{\ell},x_{t})\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta_{\ell},x_{t})}{p_{C}(y\mid h_{t-1},x_{t})}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Therefore,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x_{t};h_{t-1}).}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>exp</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x_{t};h_{t-1}).}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS4.p4.3" class="ltx_p">That is, the expected reward is not an estimator of the one-step EIG: it is
the one-step EIG itself under the finite contrastive model. Equivalently,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\mathbb{E}\!\left[r_{t}^{\mathrm{real}}\mid h_{t-1},x_{t}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>exp</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>real</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}^{\mathrm{exp}}=\mathbb{E}\!\left[r_{t}^{\mathrm{real}}\mid h_{t-1},x_{t}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS4.p4.4" class="ltx_p">Consequently, under the matched model the two rewards have the same expectation,
while marginalizing over hypotheses and outcomes removes the variance arising
from sampling <math id="A4.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\theta^{\star},y_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\theta^{\star},y_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.5 </span>When the Training-Target Distribution Differs from the Contrastive Prior</h3>

<div id="A4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The distinction between realized and expected rewards becomes important when
the distribution used to generate training targets differs from the prior used
to define the information objective. This can arise naturally when a large
contrastive set is used to provide a rich information-gain signal, while
training trajectories are generated for only a subset of hypotheses for
computational efficiency.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the distribution of realized training targets, with
<math id="A4.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{supp}(q)\subseteq\Theta_{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>supp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>C</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{supp}(q)\subseteq\Theta_{C}</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="A4.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{C}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{C}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> remains the prior used
by the contrastive reward model. At a fixed history <math id="A4.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>, let</p>
<table id="A4.Ex29" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{h}(\theta)=q(\theta\mid h)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{h}(\theta)=q(\theta\mid h)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">denote the corresponding posterior over realized training targets. The two
models induce posterior-predictive distributions</p>
<table id="A4.Ex30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{q}(y\mid h,x)=\sum_{\theta}q_{h}(\theta)p(y\mid\theta,x)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>θ</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{q}(y\mid h,x)=\sum_{\theta}q_{h}(\theta)p(y\mid\theta,x),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p2.3" class="ltx_p">and</p>
<table id="A4.Ex31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{C}(y\mid h,x)=\sum_{\theta}p_{C}(\theta\mid h)p(y\mid\theta,x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>θ</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{C}(y\mid h,x)=\sum_{\theta}p_{C}(\theta\mid h)p(y\mid\theta,x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Consider the same realized reward,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\mathrm{real}}=\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta,x)}{p_{C}(y\mid h,x)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>real</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\mathrm{real}}=\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta,x)}{p_{C}(y\mid h,x)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p3.2" class="ltx_p">but now take its expectation under the training-target distribution
<math id="A4.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{h}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{h}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.Ex33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex33.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim q_{h},\,y\sim p(\cdot\mid\theta,x)}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>h</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>real</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim q_{h},\,y\sim p(\cdot\mid\theta,x)}[r^{\mathrm{real}}].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Adding and subtracting <math id="A4.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p_{q}(y\mid h,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p_{q}(y\mid h,x)</annotation></semantics></math> gives</p>
<table id="A4.Ex34" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.Ex34X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex34X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{q}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>real</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{q}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex34X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{q_{h}(\theta)p(y\mid\theta,x)}\left[\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta,x)}{p_{q}(y\mid h,x)}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{q_{h}(\theta)p(y\mid\theta,x)}\left[\log\frac{p(y\mid\theta,x)}{p_{q}(y\mid h,x)}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="A4.Ex34Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex34Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_{q}(\cdot\mid h,x)}\left[\log\frac{p_{q}(y\mid h,x)}{p_{C}(y\mid h,x)}\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>[</mo><mi>log</mi><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_{q}(\cdot\mid h,x)}\left[\log\frac{p_{q}(y\mid h,x)}{p_{C}(y\mid h,x)}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="A4.Ex34Xb"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex34Xb.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{EIG}_{q}(x;h)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p_{q}(Y\mid h,x)\;\|\;p_{C}(Y\mid h,x)\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>EIG</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>KL</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="0.447em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{EIG}_{q}(x;h)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p_{q}(Y\mid h,x)\;\|\;p_{C}(Y\mid h,x)\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p3.4" class="ltx_p">Hence,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\mathbb{E}_{q}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]=\mathrm{EIG}_{q}(x;h)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p_{q}(Y\mid h,x)\|p_{C}(Y\mid h,x)\right).}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>real</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>EIG</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>KL</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\mathbb{E}_{q}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]=\mathrm{EIG}_{q}(x;h)+D_{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p_{q}(Y\mid h,x)\|p_{C}(Y\mid h,x)\right).}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The second term vanishes when the training-target distribution and contrastive
model induce the same predictive distribution. Otherwise, the expected
realized reward does not equal the EIG of the contrastive model: it additionally
rewards disagreement between the predictive distribution induced by the
training targets and that induced by the contrastive prior.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">By contrast, the expected reward continues to marginalize using the
contrastive model itself:</p>
<table id="A4.Ex36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex36.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="r^{\mathrm{exp}}(h,x)=\mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim p_{C}(\theta\mid h),\,y\sim p(\cdot\mid\theta,x)}[r^{\mathrm{real}}]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>exp</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>C</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>real</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\mathrm{exp}}(h,x)=\mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim p_{C}(\theta\mid h),\,y\sim p(\cdot\mid\theta,x)}[r^{\mathrm{real}}],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p5.2" class="ltx_p">and therefore remains</p>
<table id="A4.Ex37" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{r^{\mathrm{exp}}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x;h)}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mi>exp</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{r^{\mathrm{exp}}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x;h)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p5.3" class="ltx_p">regardless of the empirical distribution from which training targets were
sampled.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The training-target distribution can still affect which histories are visited.
If <math id="A4.SS5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{q}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{q}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the state distribution induced by training targets sampled
from <math id="A4.SS5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, then expected-reward training optimizes</p>
<table id="A4.Ex38" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex38.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d_{q},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x;h)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d_{q},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[\mathrm{EIG}_{C}(x;h)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS5.p6.2" class="ltx_p">Thus, <math id="A4.SS5.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> controls the distribution of training states, while <math id="A4.SS5.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{C}</annotation></semantics></math> controls
what constitutes an informative design at each state.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.6 </span>Decoupling the Generative Model from the Policy</h3>

<div id="A4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Estimating information gain requires specifying a generative model</p>
<table id="A4.Ex39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=\{p_{G}(\theta),\,p_{G}(y\mid\theta,x)\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=\{p_{G}(\theta),\,p_{G}(y\mid\theta,x)\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">A key design choice is whether this model is specified independently of the
policy or induced by the policy itself.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">External generative model.</span>
In our setting, the generative model <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed independently of the policy
parameters <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>. It therefore defines a fixed information reward</p>
<table id="A4.Ex40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex40.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{G}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{G}(x;h)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{G}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{G}(x;h).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The value of this reward varies across histories and designs, but the criterion
used to evaluate a particular <math id="A4.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(h,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(h,x)</annotation></semantics></math> does not change as the policy is updated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\pi_{\phi}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\pi_{\phi}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the distribution over histories induced by the
current policy. The one-step training objective can then be written as</p>
<table id="A4.Ex41" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex41.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d^{\pi_{\phi}},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[r_{G}(h,x)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d^{\pi_{\phi}},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[r_{G}(h,x)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Thus, the policy parameters affect which histories are visited and which
designs are proposed, while the information objective used to score those
designs remains fixed.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, writing <math id="A4.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> for a trajectory and <math id="A4.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{G}(\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{G}(\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> for its
information return,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex42" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex42.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}(\tau)}\left[R_{G}(\tau)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}(\tau)}\left[R_{G}(\tau)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A4.SS6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{G}</annotation></semantics></math> has no direct dependence on <math id="A4.SS6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex43" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\phi}J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[R_{G}(\tau)\,\nabla_{\phi}\log p_{\phi}(\tau)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>G</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\phi}J_{G}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[R_{G}(\tau)\,\nabla_{\phi}\log p_{\phi}(\tau)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p4.3" class="ltx_p">Hence policy learning changes the distribution over trajectories, but not the
information measure against which those trajectories are evaluated.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Policy-induced generative model.</span>
Alternatively, the same LLM being optimized may also be used to define the
experimental generative model, for example through</p>
<table id="A4.Ex44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex44.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\phi}(\theta\mid h)\qquad\text{and/or}\qquad p_{\phi}(y\mid\theta,x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mtext>and/or</mtext><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\phi}(\theta\mid h)\qquad\text{and/or}\qquad p_{\phi}(y\mid\theta,x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p5.2" class="ltx_p">The resulting information reward is then itself parameterized by the policy,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex45.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\phi}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{G_{\phi}}(x;h)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>EIG</mi><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\phi}(h,x)=\mathrm{EIG}_{G_{\phi}}(x;h),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p5.3" class="ltx_p">and the objective becomes</p>
<table id="A4.Ex46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex46.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d^{\pi_{\phi}},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[r_{\phi}(h,x)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></msup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{h\sim d^{\pi_{\phi}},\,x\sim\pi_{\phi}(\cdot\mid h)}\left[r_{\phi}(h,x)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In this case, updating <math id="A4.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> has two conceptually distinct effects:
it changes both
(i) which histories and designs are generated by the policy, and
(ii) the generative model used to assign information value to those designs.
At the trajectory level,</p>
<table id="A4.Ex47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}(\tau)}\left[R_{\phi}(\tau)\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}(\tau)}\left[R_{\phi}(\tau)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS6.p6.2" class="ltx_p">whose full gradient is</p>
<table id="A4.Ex48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex48.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boxed{\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)=\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[R_{\phi}(\tau)\nabla_{\phi}\log p_{\phi}(\tau)\right]}_{\text{policy-selection effect}}+\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[\nabla_{\phi}R_{\phi}(\tau)\right]}_{\text{reward-model effect}}.}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>policy-selection effect</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>reward-model effect</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boxed{\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)=\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[R_{\phi}(\tau)\nabla_{\phi}\log p_{\phi}(\tau)\right]}_{\text{policy-selection effect}}+\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim p_{\phi}}\left[\nabla_{\phi}R_{\phi}(\tau)\right]}_{\text{reward-model effect}}.}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The first term improves the policy with respect to its current information
criterion. The second reflects the fact that changing the policy also changes
the criterion itself, through changes to the policy-induced prior and/or
likelihood.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS6.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS6.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS6.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implication.</span>
Decoupling the experimental generative model from the policy removes this
second source of dependence. The policy is therefore optimized against a
stationary information objective: training may change which states are visited
and which designs are proposed, but it does not simultaneously change what
constitutes an informative design.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</article>
</div>
</div>
